PullRequest.Title: sessions: enlarge the mobile host Refresh touch target
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Bring the phone host picker's Refresh control up to the existing touch-target
baseline. Its current 32px height is smaller than the surrounding phone controls.
The same minimum applies while it displays Searching.

This is the host Refresh portion of mobile audit finding F6. The Sort Close
control is already addressed independently in #348979. Discovery, connection
behavior, keyboard handling and labels are unchanged.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp -- compile-client` — passed, zero errors.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/mobileHostPickerStyles.test.ts --browser chromium` — **3 passed**.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/mobileHostPickerStyles.test.ts` — **4 passed**.
- `git diff --check` and normal commit hygiene hooks — passed.
- `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" npm run bundle-mobile` — passed
  unchanged policy at `c65754b2bfd4fde3b07adc1d5a71a30e078923ad`.

The two new geometry regressions failed at the original height. At 320px and
390px they check both Refresh and Searching, at least 44px dimensions, all four
hit edges, viewport fit and separation from adjacent host rows. The fixture
uses synthetic controls with the production styles; no live discovery or
connection was performed. Direct bounded source review found no blocker.

| Measurement | gzip bytes | Unchanged limit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Initial | 6,308,725 | 7,000,000 |
| Main JavaScript | 5,702,211 | 6,400,000 |
| CSS | 242,853 | 275,000 |
| Runtime | 14,710,356 | 16,500,000 |
| Extensions | 712,868 | 800,000 |

Manual follow-up: open the phone computer picker and tap the edges of Refresh.
Confirm the control stays usable while searching and does not overlap a row.
Physical iOS/Safari and live discovery remain unvalidated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the mobile host picker, display host rows, and switch the Refresh control between idle and Searching.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: show() synchronously builds the sheet and renders the existing host list before display/focus. The changed CSS changes minimum dimensions for one section action from 32px tall to at least 44px tall and wide. Opening does not initiate discovery or wait for network operations.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Refresh action per open sheet; existing row rendering scales with the number of known hosts. The diff adds no elements, listeners, collection iterations, or geometry reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser DOM/style/layout work. An already-open sheet is guarded against reopening; no new parallel work is scheduled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both cold and warm opens use the filter service's existing host state. The action is retained while host lists rerender; subscriptions and row stores retain their existing disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected the complete CSS diff, its only production consumer, sheet construction, refresh updates, and mobile target token definition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Device-specific layout timing was not measured, but a constant-size change to one existing control establishes no additional scaling or repeated-layout mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Two minimum-size declarations do not introduce new rendering loops, forced layout reads, discovery calls, or resource retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Tap Refresh and wait for computer discovery to finish.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The unchanged click/tap handler calls rediscover only when isDiscovering is false. rediscover starts registered discovery handlers and awaits Promise.allSettled; the UI remains usable while Searching is displayed. The tunnel handler awaits authentication and account-level enumeration before publishing refreshed host state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query authentication sessions through the authentication service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two configured providers are tried sequentially, with a scoped query and an optional fallback session query per provider; the last successful provider is tried first. This is per discovery, not per host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical authentication selection, query count, ordering, and silent behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication must resolve before direct browser tunnel enumeration; silent discovery does not create an interactive authentication session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dynamically import the browser Dev Tunnels SDK bundle on first use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A module-level promise coalesces loading across callers; no repeated SDK import on warm refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical lazy loading and promise reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold direct-browser discovery waits for the SDK after authentication; warm discovery reuses the promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call managementClient.listTunnels with the launcher label and filter returned tunnel information.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical account-level SDK enumeration per eligible tunnel discovery, independent of the number of displayed host rows. Underlying SDK request count is not established by repository code inspected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same account-level enumeration occurred once per eligible refresh; CSS dimensions do not alter call frequency or grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery completion waits for enumeration. It does not block initial sheet opening.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Alternatively delegate enumeration to the embedder's discovery provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider.listTunnels call per eligible discovery when the embedder implementation is selected, instead of direct browser SDK enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical delegate selection, call count, and awaiting behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery completion waits for the embedder result; internal embedder transport is outside the inspected repository implementation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered discovery handler count controls concurrent logical discoveries; tunnel result count controls unchanged filtering, cache reconciliation, and host-row updates. Neither boundary is invoked per rendered row by the changed code.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: rediscover invokes registered handlers concurrently using Promise.allSettled. The Refresh handler suppresses another request while any discovery is active; within direct-browser tunnel discovery authentication, SDK readiness, and enumeration are awaited in sequence. No limiter or coalescing behavior changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The host cache supplies existing entries but does not suppress explicit tunnel enumeration. Direct-browser SDK loading is promise-cached, authentication favors the last successful provider, and discovery failure preserves cached tunnels. None of these behaviors changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the unchanged action guard through rediscover, tunnel contribution, browser/embedder selection, authentication, SDK loader, and enumeration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency, account tunnel counts, other handler costs, and embedder internals vary, but the diff introduces no additional call or critical-path dependency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The expanded hit area changes neither discovery cardinality nor concurrency, caching, network behavior, or waiting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Execute the added mobile host-picker geometry tests at 320px and 390px.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each test creates a small synthetic DOM fixture, checks two label states, and synchronously reads geometry and hit testing before assertions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two new width cases and two action states per case, with three synthetic buttons and four edge hit tests per state; no live discovery or connection is invoked.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Bounded synchronous test callbacks. Geometry reads after label/class writes can cause layout within these tests, not on a newly introduced production path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The added production stylesheet import is test-only. Fixtures are removed through the existing disposable test store; no new persistent cache or production dependency is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected the complete test diff and surrounding suite lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional test runtime is unmeasured but bounded by four small fixture states, with no realistic unbounded or hot production trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added layout work is deliberately bounded test coverage and is not shipped application work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 36e8c0289a5f29eae15a933263220d9895302ff6. Inspected both changed files and all diff pages, traced production rendering and refresh boundaries, and found no high-confidence performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix requiring provenance collection. Review was static; no runtime profiling was performed.
